    New baby in the house or on the way? Fort Worth Moms is pleased to offer “Breastfeeding Resources in the Fort Worth Area” to help you find and navigate the many local resources available to your family.  

    Got more questions about breastfeeding? Check out our guides below:

    • Breastfeeding Resources in the Collin County Area
    • Breastfeeding Resources in the Dallas Area
    • Breastfeeding Resources in the Denton County Area

    Get this and other hyperlocal resources delivered to your inbox by joining the Fort Worth Moms subscriber list. You can also join one or more of our Fort Worth Moms community groups. We also produce the Momfessions Podcast. Listen today!

    Follow along on our socials:

    Laura - August 8, 2026 0

    Soothe Your Weary Nipples :: A Lactation Consultant Answers All Your Breastfeeding Questions

    Amanda - August 9, 2026 0
    Breastfeeding didn’t come easily to me. I fretted about everything: Is she getting enough milk? Why is she nursing so often? Why does it hurt so much when everything I’ve read told me it shouldn’t hurt? Am I eating the right things? Are my boobs destined to look like missiles from now on? In a fit of defeat, I contacted a lactation consultant, and that decision made all the difference in the world.

    8 Things I’d Tell a First-Time Mom About Breastfeeding

So if you’re experiencing that now, I see you. Here are tips, perspective, and gentle advice for a first-time breastfeeding mom.

    Breastfeeding Success: The One Thing You Must Have

    Julie - August 1, 2017 2
    Then I had my first baby. And you know what I found? Breastfeeding was so hard. Physically hard. Emotionally hard. That baby had a terrible latch. I couldn't pump enough milk to cover the bottom of a bottle. I was exhausted and hormonal. And I knew that all of those breastfeeding supplies meant nothing if I didn't have the one thing I really needed . . . a healthy dose of plain old stubbornness.

      Jennifer
      Jennifer Waldon is a devoted wife and mother of two vibrant girls. Though she grew up in Louisiana, she met her husband (a native Texan) there and has since spent the last two decades embracing life in Texas. Jennifer is a proud Native American woman who is passionate about her culture. Her creative outlets include writing and learning cultural history. When she needs a break, she escapes into the pages of a good romance novel. Above all, her greatest commitment is to her family and encouraging her daughters to try new things and discover their own passions.
